title: Castle Mountains National Monument: Most Monument Roads Require Heavy Duty 4WD Vehicle to Travel Safely
summary: Breaking down in the remote monument can be a life-threatening emergency. Most roads require a well-equipped, heavy-duty 4WD vehicle to travel. 2WD high clearance vehicles must use Walking Box Ranch Rd for entry and exit. No Visitor Facilities Available.

title: Castle Mountains National Monument: No Hunting Allowed in Castle Mountains National Monument
summary: Hunting is illegal in Castle Mountains National Monument

title: Mojave National Preserve: Delays up to 1 hour are possible at Kelbaker Road Railroad Crossing near Kelso Depot
summary: In the event there are train siding operations at the crossing near Kelso Depot, delays may be up to one hour. Please plan accordingly for this possibility with extra fuel and drinking water. Union Pacific Contact: 1 800 848-8715

title: Mojave National Preserve: Kelso Depot Visitor Center closed
summary: Kelso Depot Visitor Center is closed for rehabilitation of the heating and cooling system. We expect to reopen the depot in 2026. The restrooms beside the depot are open.

title: Mojave National Preserve: Do not pick up hitchhikers
summary: Do not pick up hitchhikers. Please report their locations to law enforcement by calling 911.

title: Mojave National Preserve: NPS Visitor Wi-Fi
summary: Visitor Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi calling is now available in the Kelso Depot parking lot for calls including emergencies. Go to the bulletin board at the Kelso Depot restrooms for instructions.

title: Lake Mead National Recreation Area: Government Wash and 8.0 Mile Road Anticipated Reopening
summary: The Government Wash campground and 8.0 Mile Road are anticipated to reopen in late November to vehicle access and overnight camping. This alert will be updated once the reopening date has been set.

title: Mojave National Preserve: Road Damage/Debris on Road
summary: Use caution when driving through Mojave National Preserve. Widespread storms have flooded, damaged and deposited debris on roads throughout the preserve.

title: Castle Mountains National Monument
summary: Castle Mountains represents some of the most unique elements of the Mojave Desert. Nestled between the Nevada state line and Mojave National Preserve, the nearly 21,000 acres of Castle Mountains boasts Joshua tree forests, unbroken natural landscapes, rare desert grasslands, and rich human history. This intriguing area provides serenity and solitude from nearby metropolitan areas.

title: Lake Mead National Recreation Area
summary: Experience outdoor thrills, striking landscapes, and brilliant blue waters. This year-round recreation area spreads across 1.5 million acres of mountains, canyons, valleys and two vast reservoirs. Visitors come here for scenic drives, biking, hiking, boating, fishing, camping, and much more.

title: Mojave National Preserve
summary: Mojave preserves a diverse mosaic of ecological habitats and a 10,000 year history of human connection with the desert. Offering extensive opportunities to experience desert landscapes, the preserve promotes understanding and appreciation for the increasingly threatened resources of the Mojave Desert. This remote preserve encourages a sense of discovery and a connection to wild places.
